{"draft": "Capital One Q2 2026: Profit Rebounds, Revenue Growth Continues
Capital One delivered net income of $3.0 billion, or $4.73 per diluted common share, while adjusted net income came to $5.81 per diluted common share.
Total net revenue rose 4 percent to $15.9 billion, helped by a net interest margin of 8.01 percent that expanded 14 basis points. Total non-interest expense climbed 7 percent to $9.0 billion, reflecting an 11 percent jump in marketing and a 6 percent increase in operating expenses, leaving pre-provision earnings up 1 percent at $6.8 billion.
Credit costs eased, with the provision for credit losses down $1.1 billion to $3.0 billion. That result included net charge-offs of $3.6 billion and a $662 million loan reserve release, suggesting a more benign credit backdrop during the quarter.
On the balance sheet, period-end loans held for investment grew $9.4 billion, or 2 percent, to $457.2 billion, with Credit Card period-end loans reaching $275.4 billion and loan growth also recorded across consumer and commercial banking. The common equity Tier 1 capital ratio stood at 13.7%, while period-end total deposits were $484.3 billion.
Outlook: The release gives no formal guidance, so the focus remains on the Discover integration, the sustainability of revenue and margin momentum, expense discipline, credit-loss trends and capital strength."}
